## 2024-11-04 - [CRITICAL] Command Injection via JSON.stringify in Bash Exec
**Vulnerability:** Command substitution injection in bash exec calls (`$(cmd)`). When paths were passed into `exec` using `JSON.stringify(wanted)`, the double quotes generated by JSON allowed bash to execute nested commands.
**Learning:** `JSON.stringify` does not provide safe shell quoting. While it quotes strings for JSON parsing, double-quoted strings in bash allow variable and command expansion (`$VAR`, `$(cmd)`).
**Prevention:** Strictly use single-quote escaping for shell commands: `'\'' + str.replace(/'/g, "'\\''") + '\''`. Single quotes prevent bash from evaluating any substitutions.
